title: Respiratory signals supported retrospective COVID-19 ICU risk stratification
summary: A Gaussian mixture model grouped respiratory-rate and oxygen-saturation signals from 279 ICU patients with COVID-19 to estimate intubation risk and a 24-hour severity score. The study reports 87.8% intubation recognition (AUC 0.94), three score-associated risk groups, and 81.0% accuracy for ICU stays over five days at a score threshold above 40. It is a retrospective single-setting result, not evidence of improved care or transportability.
organization: Aix-Marseille Université; Assistance Publique–Hôpitaux de Marseille; Laveran Military Teaching Hospital

evidence.tested: Retrospective data from one French ICU across two pandemic periods; outcomes were observed intubation and length of stay. No prospective clinical-impact evaluation is reported.
evidence.unknown: No independent, prospective or clinical-impact evaluation is reported unless specified in the tested field.
evidence.ai_role: The unsupervised model clustered oxygen-saturation and respiratory-rate signals and derived hourly intubation probabilities summarized as a severity score.
